name: Helianthus

study_strategy.warning: Many Asteraceae look similar from a distance. Use head structure and involucre details, not just a yellow flower photo.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Confirm a true sunflower head: many disk florets on one receptacle, yellow ray florets around the margin, and an involucre of green phyllaries beneath. Then use whole-plant architecture and leaves before tightening to phyllaries.
shared_traits: yellow ray florets surrounding many disk florets
involucre of phyllaries beneath each head
flattened cypselae that may carry short awns
shared_genus_recognition.caution: A yellow radiate Asteraceae head is not enough for Helianthus. Confirm the capitulum/involucre, then use leaves, branching pattern and phyllaries.

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: rhizomatous perennial; often colonial and more upright with less free branching

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: broad ovate to deltoid-ovate, rough; lower leaves often long-petiolate
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: numerous narrow linear-lanceolate rough leaves, often folded lengthwise and curving downward

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: lower leaves opposite, upper leaves alternate
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: mostly alternate; lower leaves can be opposite/subopposite

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: usually several to many heads on branching stems
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: many heads in elongated inflorescences on tall upright stems

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: broader lanceolate to ovate, ciliate-hispid, spreading to somewhat reflexed
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: long and narrow, ascending to spreading

species_key.if: broad ovate/deltoid rough leaves on a usually branching annual
many narrow linear-lanceolate leaves, commonly conduplicate/folded and curving downward on an upright perennial

overlap_and_cautions: Do not use yellow ray color or dark-versus-light disk color as the primary split.
Lower leaves of H. maximiliani can be opposite/subopposite, so leaf arrangement alone is not decisive.
Both species can be tall, rough, multi-headed and 2-awned in fruit.
Young or mowed plants may hide the annual-versus-colonial architecture; in those cases prioritize leaf proportions/folding plus mature phyllaries.

local_lookalike_routing.separate: First prove Helianthus-like head structure and involucre; then compare leaf arrangement, receptacle/phyllaries and fruit rather than flower color.
Do not route from height or yellow heads. Use leaf architecture/attachment and head underside; if those structures are missing, stop at the broader composite comparison.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: branching annual H. annuus versus upright/colonial H. maximiliani
broad ovate/deltoid versus narrow linear-lanceolate; show petiole/attachment and any lengthwise fold
compare broad ciliate-hispid versus long narrow phyllaries
teach lower-opposite-to-upper-alternate transition in H. annuus and mostly alternate pattern in H. maximiliani without overclaiming
confirm shared sunflower fruit architecture; not a primary species separator

targeted_handoff.diagnostic_photo_polish: Acquire/label matched leaf and head-underside pairs before adding decorative gallery images.
targeted_handoff.taxonomy_diagnostic_review: No new taxonomy/range issue opened; if a specimen lacks mature leaves/phyllaries or presents intermediate architecture, do not force species from color/height alone.
